papers.title_en: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
papers.authors: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu, Hao Xiao, Shuhan Xue, Qiang Gao, Wanli Ouyang, Pheng Ann Heng, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu, Ling Yang
papers.evidence: 由预测式世界模型引导的领域通用递归自我改进框架
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进需要将交互经验转为持续提升，但外部反馈昂贵，且策略演化会使世界模型预测失准。RSI-Anything基于JEPA-Anything，用预测性世界模型指导动作与学习数据选择，并以反馈驱动策略/工作流改进和世界模型条件适配。代码修复成功率由26.3%升至31.2%，GUI平均动作减少39.4%，实验室规划分数从21.80%增至46.01%，反应优化达96.15%平均最佳产率。该框架通过组件与兼容性检查保留更新后的策略-模型对，实现跨领域递归改进。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) aims to transform interaction experience into persistent improvements, yet external feedback is costly and world-model predictions may become unreliable as policies evolve. We introduce RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework built on JEPA-Anything that uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection. Observed feedback drives policy or workflow improvement and conditional world-model adaptation, while component and compatibility checks govern the retention of updated policy-model pairs. Across diverse computational and scientific domains, RSI-Anything demonstrates substantial gains. In code repair, with the coder fixed, success increases from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% through predictive selection and 31.2% after world-model adaptation, at comparable test usage. Graphical user interface (GUI) evaluations showed higher task completion, while average actions decrease by 39.4%. Across five successive policy versions, laboratory-planning scores more than double from 21.80% to 46.01%. In reaction optimization, RSI-Anything achieves 96.15% mean best observed yield versus 82.16% for Bayesian optimization under the same 40-experiment budget. An end-to-end immune-science application further connects workflow evolution and predictive modeling with therapeutic hypothesis generation. These results demonstrate how predictive world models and retained system updates enable recursive improvement across diverse environments.

papers.title_en: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
papers.authors: Zhipeng Chen, Yunsen Liang, Yanxi Chen, Hongkang Zhao, Lingyun Feng, Ruiyang Ren, Guoxin Chen, Jia Deng, Feng Chang, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Jian Yang, Ji-Rong Wen, Bryan Dai, Wayne Xin Zhao
papers.evidence: 定义递归自我改进并构建在动态环境中从自身经验持续进化的智能体系统
papers.tldr: 现有AI多依赖冻结参数与外部更新，难以在持续变化且可验证的真实环境中实现递归自我改进。DeepEvolve以未来事件预测构建开放世界，动态合成可验证任务，并用递归进化引擎将预测推理轨迹转化为能力，借搜索与预测解耦及技能蒸馏适应在线污染。它在FutureX周榜连续三周居所有系统第一、评分最高提升195%，合成评测在四个基座LLM上均进前三。这表明自我改进智能体需与开放世界共同进化，推动AI从静态训练转向经验驱动成长。
papers.abstract_en: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet studying RSI requires an environment that is continuously changing, objectively verifiable, and naturally grounded, posing a fundamental challenge for agent evolution. Here we introduce DeepEvolve, a sustainable evolution agent system grounded in future event prediction, in which agents continuously interact with a dynamically evolving environment and improve by internalizing and externalizing the experience gained through these interactions. A living environment synthesizes verifiable tasks, and a recursive-evolution engine turns the reasoning trajectory behind each prediction back into capability: decoupling search from prediction adapts parameter-level evolution to the contamination-prone live environment, while distilling reusable skills lets the agent evolve from the limited live trajectories such an environment affords. On the external FutureX leaderboard, which evaluates predictions against real-world outcomes and is updated weekly, our self-improved forecaster ranked first across all systems over three consecutive weeks, achieving up to a 195% improvement in rating. On our synthesized evaluation, it ranked among the top three across four base LLMs, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 10.7 Bradley--Terry points. More broadly, these results suggest that a system built for self-improvement is best understood as an agent that co-evolves with a genuinely living, open-ended environment, pointing to a shift in AI from training static models on fixed data toward cultivating agents that grow stronger from their own experience, with such an open world as the indispensable basis of that growth.

papers.title_en: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
papers.authors: Yue Huang, Yanbo Wang, Lichi Li, Yuanyuan Chen, Andreas Haupt, Xiaonan Luo, Zheyuan Liu, Jihye Choi, Felix Juefei-Xu, Xiangliang Zhang, Radha Poovendran, Misha Sra, Ying Liu, Ben Burtenshaw, Thomas Wolf, Alex Pentland, Zichen Chen, Zhangchen Xu
papers.evidence: 研究AI智能体自主后训练并改进语言模型以迈向递归自我改进
papers.tldr: 为检验AI能否自主后训练语言模型并用人类反馈持续改进，RSI Arena让十个前沿模型作为训练代理，从Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base出发，在共享64-GPU集群上自主选数据、实现训练流程并挑选检查点。第一阶段六天内十个代理均产出可用助手，最佳模型在12项能力基准上弥合基座到Instruct中位差距的76%，盲评偏好经长度与格式校正后接近NVIDIA Instruct。第二阶段加入比较记录和投票再训练三天，十个模型中有八个风格校正相对评分提升。该工作提供可审计环境，研究人类反馈如何引导自主模型开发，迈向RSIHF。
papers.abstract_en: Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We introduce RSI Arena, a two-stage study of autonomous post-training as a step toward recursive self-improvement. Ten frontier models act as training agents, each starting from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base. During a six-day first stage, each agent has 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 in API credit on a shared 64-GPU cluster, independently selecting data, implementing training procedures, and choosing checkpoints. We evaluate their models on 20 benchmarks and through blind human evaluations. All ten agents produce working assistants, with the strongest model, trained by GPT-6 Astra, closing a median of 76% of the base-to-Instruct gap across 12 capability benchmarks. Its human-preference rating is also close to NVIDIA Instruct after statistical adjustment for answer length and formatting. In Stage 2, each agent receives the comparison records and votes involving its Stage 1 model and is given three additional days for further training. Using NVIDIA Instruct as a common reference across the two evaluation rounds, we observe an improvement from Stage 1 to Stage 2 in the style-adjusted relative rating of eight of the ten models. We show that benchmark gains were modest, with no clear link to preference gains, while some agents encouraged longer responses and one model showed increased harmful compliance on StrongREJECT. RSI Arena provides an auditable setting for studying how human feedback can guide autonomous model development. It takes a step toward recursive self-improvement with human feedback (RSIHF), in which people help define what improvement means for the AI systems they use.

papers.title_en: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
papers.authors: Weidong Tang, Ruiheng Wang, Jingxuan Zhang, Hexin Wang, Haoyuan Chen, Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Yixing Ma, Zichen Jiang, Ziyu Guo, Haodong Li, Zhengbo Jiao, Zhiqing Cui, Xinxiang Yin, Shuo Liang, Zhenglin Wan, Hongzhan Lin, Wangbo Zhao Kaipeng Zhang, Pengfei Zhou, Odin Zhang, Yang You
papers.evidence: 耦合世界生成与框架演化的递归自我改进框架
papers.tldr: 多模态智能可视为世界与智能体在人类引导下通过交互协同演化，但异构可验证环境构建成本高，人工Harness迭代也难跟上任务多样性与复杂度。The Trinity用Creator、Explorer、Evolver三角色递归耦合世界生成与Harness演化，依据已验证轨迹把任务树重组为分层能力树，并以Real2Sim2Real抽象可验证模拟世界、选择性继承能力模块。不同Harness专精不同能力，由能力感知路由器按公开任务信息选择配置；在28个训练基准平均提升34分，18个未见基准提升26分，并覆盖两个真实具身任务。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.

papers.title_en: EmbodiRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Data-Efficient Robot Adaptation
papers.authors: Haoran Lang, Haotao Lu, Shiyu Sang, Haoyang Luo, Guo Chen, Qun Li, Jingyi Yu, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang
papers.evidence: 面向数据高效机器人策略适配的智能体式递归自我改进系统
papers.tldr: 机器人策略适配新任务通常依赖大量真实数据，且所需数据取决于当前策略能力与失败模式。EmbodiRSI 构建任务特定仿真，以执行反馈驱动协作纠错和自适应数据采集，在真实-仿真-真实循环中递归改进策略。实验在3个桌面环境和14个子任务上，将仿真场景平衡成功率从50.4%提升到83.5%，并用少量真实数据达到83.1%真实成功率。这表明面向部署场景的反馈驱动递归自我改进可实现数据高效的机器人适配。
papers.abstract_en: Adapting robot manipulation policies to new tasks and environments remains highly data-intensive, while the data needed for further improvement depends on the policy's current capabilities and failure modes. We introduce EmbodiRSI, an agentic system for recursive self-improvement (RSI) in a real-to-sim-to-real setting, where task-specific simulations are constructed from target deployment scenarios and used as low-cost environments for iterative policy improvement before transfer back to the physical world. EmbodiRSI uses policy execution feedback to guide subsequent experience acquisition and policy updates. Two complementary mechanisms close this loop: Collaborative Error Correction generates agent-assisted corrective trajectories from policy-reached states, while Adaptive Data Collection directs expert demonstration generation toward the current policy's weaknesses. The task-specific simulation serves as a reusable workspace for policy warm-up, repeatable evaluation, failure diagnosis, and targeted data generation across successive RSI rounds. Across three tabletop environments and 14 subtasks, EmbodiRSI increases scene-balanced autonomous simulation success from 50.4% to 83.5% over two RSI updates. With 400 adaptive simulated trajectories and only ten real-world refinement trajectories per subtask, EmbodiRSI achieves 83.1% scene-balanced autonomous real-world success, compared with 75.0% for adaptation using 200 real-world demonstrations per subtask. These results demonstrate that feedback-driven recursive improvement in deployment-specific simulations can enable data-efficient adaptation of embodied policies to physical environments.

papers.title_en: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Design Their Own Evaluations?
papers.authors: Yaolun Zhang, Tianyi Xu, Yujie Zhao, Jishen Zhao, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang
papers.evidence: 面向 AI 智能体自动化评测设计的基准，支撑递归自我改进
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进依赖评测反馈，但反复运行复杂基准成本高、拖慢迭代。EvalResearchBench 让“researcher”智能体在固定时间和 API 预算下选择或合成任务、实现并修订评分器，最终冻结可执行评测器。实验覆盖9个researcher与13个候选模型，最优评测器在约75%的候选对上与14个目标基准排序一致，低于目标间91%的上限。结果显示智能体可自动化评测设计，但尚无全能方案，开发集最优未必迁移到封存目标，低成本评测器反而成对一致性最高。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) relies on evaluation feedback to assess progress and guide further research, yet repeatedly running complex benchmarks is costly and slows iteration. Human experts reduce this cost by selecting benchmark subsets or designing compact suites. We ask whether AI agents can automate this design process and introduce EvalResearchBench (ERB), a benchmark for autonomous evaluation research. Given target materials, development references, candidate APIs, and fixed time and API budgets, an agent called the researcher selects or synthesizes tasks, implements graders, and revises them in pilot tests before freezing an executable evaluator for coding, co-work, and reasoning. We study 9 researchers and 13 candidate models and compare each frozen evaluator with 14 target benchmarks on score concordance and pairwise agreement. The best evaluators order about 75\% of candidate pairs as the targets do, below the 91\% ceiling set by disagreements among the targets. No researcher leads on every metric, and the best evaluator on development targets is not the best on sealed targets hidden from the researcher. A human-designed sample of public tasks remains a strong baseline, and the evaluator with the lowest recorded execution cost attains the highest pairwise agreement. Agents repair tasks and graders through pilot feedback, yet their evaluators can still truncate answers, exhaust the evaluation budget, or let a few questions dominate a domain score.

papers.title_en: RSI-Forge: From Research Papers to Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.authors: Renxiong Wang, Darvin Yi, Abril Herrlein, Anas Mahmoud, Advait Gosai, Lisiman Hua, MohammadHossein Rezaei, Xingang Guo, Anisha Gunjal, Utkarsh Tyagi, David J. Lee, Minglai Yang, Haris Riaz, Chenguang Wang, Huaxiu Yao, Daniel Yue Zhang, Aakash Sabharwal, Tong Zhao, Yunzhong He
papers.evidence: 自动构建带评测器的可执行研究环境以支撑递归自我改进
papers.tldr: 构建可可靠评估的研究环境仍依赖专家，限制自改进智能体的规模化。RSI-Forge用多智能体流水线将论文转为可执行环境，由构建、复现、审查代理协作生成任务与自动评估器。它发布18个领域210个环境，其中90个经专家审查；在120个环境连续3次尝试中，至少一个模型在84%环境提升，68/120超过复现基线。该工作为训练和评估递归自改进智能体提供了可扩展路径。
papers.abstract_en: Environments are the foundation of recursive self-improvement: they provide the problems agents work on and the feedback used to evaluate progress. Yet constructing challenging research environments with reliable evaluation still depends on domain experts, limiting their scale and disciplinary coverage. We introduce RSI-Forge, a multi-agent pipeline that turns published papers into executable environments for self-improvement. Three agents coordinate construction, reproduction, and review to produce tasks with automated evaluators; each paper's method is independently reimplemented to establish a baseline score. We present 210 environments across 18 fields, including 90 reviewed by independent human domain experts. Both experts and agent judges give high ratings to the potential for improving the provided starting solutions and the evaluators' ability to distinguish solution quality, whereas experts are more critical of shortcut resistance, faithfulness to the source paper, and whether a single idea can exhaust a task. To validate their use for repeated improvement, we evaluate four models over 3 successive attempts on 120 environments, with each attempt inheriting prior code and notes while model weights remain fixed. At least one model improves after the first attempt in 84% of environments. Models also outperform the reproduced paper methods in 68 of the 120 environments, demonstrating room for gains beyond these baselines. Transcript analysis identifies work beyond parameter tuning in 95% of these successful attempts. Analysis of the resulting trajectories shows that models scoring lower on these tasks explore less, more often accept gains smaller than the reported standard error, and rely more heavily on tuning to the development set. RSI-Forge provides a scalable approach to constructing research environments for training and evaluating self-improving agents.

papers.title_en: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.authors: Fanqing Meng, Lingxiao Du, Haocheng Lu, Qiguang Chen, Ziqi Zhao, Zijian Wu, Jiayuan Zhuo, Mengkang Hu, Michael Qizhe Shieh
papers.evidence: 面向递归自我改进的智能体原生环境
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进研究要求把已接受的改动带入后续改进周期，但现有环境常让智能体重复搭建基础设施，或只能优化单个组件。作者提出基于“一切皆服务”理念的智能体原生研究环境 RSIGym，将训练、推理、采样、评估与沙箱执行封装为可复用服务，并以共享预算与权限控制支持数据、Harness 与联合三条改进轨道。定义 RSI-Index 衡量五个基准上性能差距的闭合比例，Opus 5 在联合运行中取得 0.4809 的最高值，SWE-bench Verified 从 17.67% 升至 50.33%，AIME 从 31.67% 升至 97.78%。代码与结果全部开源。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement requires carrying accepted changes into later improvement cycles, while studying agent-proposed changes also requires substantial research infrastructure. Existing settings often leave agents to rebuild routine infrastructure or restrict exploration to individual components. We introduce RSIGym, an agent-native research environment based on Everything as a Service (EaaS). RSIGym exposes training, inference, rollout, evaluation, and sandbox execution through reusable services, with shared budget and permission controls supporting Data, Harness, and Joint improvement tracks. This design enables agents to investigate individual interventions and jointly optimize data, training settings, and execution harnesses within the same environment. We define RSI-Index as the mean fraction of the remaining performance gap closed across five benchmarks covering software engineering, terminal interaction, mathematics, scientific reasoning, and skill-based tasks. Comparing six frontier research models in independent Joint runs, Opus 5 achieves the highest RSI-Index of 0.4809 under a $500 platform-service budget per benchmark run. Its selected systems improve all five benchmarks, raising SWE-bench Verified from 17.67% to 50.33% and AIME from 31.67% to 97.78%. Additional experiments examine DSH-harness refinement, budget variation, and restricted network access, while recorded trajectories reveal how agents diagnose failures and select candidates. We open-source the full RSIGym codebase and results to support reproducibility and further research.

papers.title_en: Verification and Self-Improvement in Agentic AI: Foundations and Limits
papers.authors: Chien-Ping Lu
papers.evidence: 通过有界验证与隐藏随机性区分不同自我改进机制
papers.tldr: 智能体自我提升常以性能分数衡量，难以区分搜索更久、获得额外支持与修改提议/验证机制。论文用带隐藏终端随机性的有界验证框架，把阶段、原生可达与闭包前沿形式化为可判定语言，并分析多数放大、存在性接受和精确验证。结果显示随机验证类夹在Σ_k^P与Σ_{k+1}^P之间，严格扩张需复杂性假设；有界自修改仍留在同类，选择错误另需条件误差预算。该框架将自我改进声明转化为正确性、可接受证据、验证资源与选择误差的义务。
papers.abstract_en: Agentic AI systems can improve by searching longer, receiving additional support, or modifying how they propose and verify outputs. A performance score does not distinguish these mechanisms. We compare these changes through bounded verification with hidden terminal randomness. A stage specifies admissible transcripts, polynomial bounds, an alternating verification protocol, and a terminal checker. Its native reach uses default support; its closure frontier permits all support already admitted by the interface. Under a uniform pointwise probability gap and task-relative soundness, these are well-defined languages. We prove that independent majority amplification preserves both languages, whereas existential acceptance over random tapes can admit incorrect outputs. Exact verification is the zero-randomness case, with placement and completeness results. The randomized-verifier classes satisfy $Σ_k^{\mathrm{P}}\subseteqΣ_k^{\mathrm{RV}}\subseteqΣ_{k+1}^{\mathrm{P}}$; strict enlargement and depth separation require explicit complexity assumptions, while $\mathrm{BPP}=\mathrm{P}$ yields exact companions with the same frontiers. Representation analysis separates invariant acceptance from core-versus-support labels that can change under refactoring. For recursive self-improvement, uniformly bounded self-modification under a common sound interpreter and fixed verification protocol remains within the same verification class. A separate conditional-error budget controls false selection across adaptively chosen candidates. A quota-enforced XOR-synthesis family separates unbounded ratios of search success from changes in the accepted languages; exact and probabilistic audits check the resulting evidence requirements. The framework ties self-improvement claims to obligations on correctness, admissible evidence, verification resources, and selection error.

papers.title_en: Generative Adversarial Loops
papers.authors: Kislay Aditya Oj, Nidhi Jain, Sri Surya Varma Datla, Priyanka Jayaswal, Kumar Krishna Agrawal, Aditya Desai
papers.evidence: 生成器-判别器循环自主生成对抗数据并发现算法，支撑自推进系统
papers.tldr: 当前AI研究依赖人工设定基准与方法发现，自动方法发现进展快，但自动基准与目标设定不足。论文提出生成对抗循环GAL，用判别器代理生成对抗数据暴露系统弱点，生成器代理搜索算法加以克服，并在KV压缩、稀疏视频生成、稀疏注意力和上下文扩展四类高效推理任务上验证。结果显示GAL能自主提升CompactorPress与Dual Chunk Attention等方法，在对抗数据和标准基准上均获改进。该框架为AI自主发现弱点并持续改进算法提供了路径。
papers.abstract_en: AI research progress can be viewed as the interaction between two processes: benchmark creation and method discovery. Historically, both were driven by human intelligence. However, recent advances in AI have accelerated automated method discovery, while automated benchmark creation has received comparatively less attention. To enable self-advancing systems, we propose Generative Adversarial Loop (GAL), a generator-discriminator framework alternating between two agentic searches: (1) a discriminator that generates adversarial data to expose weaknesses in current systems, and (2) a generator that discovers algorithms to overcome them. We apply this framework to approximation algorithms for efficient inference. Unlike existing auto research systems, which primarily focus on algorithm discovery, GAL introduces a discriminator agent that automates goalpost setting by continually searching for weaknesses in the current algorithm. We demonstrate adversarial data generation across four tasks: KV compression, sparse video generation, sparse attention, and context extension, where the discriminator identifies weaknesses in state of the art techniques. We further show that GAL enables autonomous improvement, with newly discovered algorithms improving not only on adversarially generated data, but also on established benchmarks. Specifically, GAL improves CompactorPress on KV compression with Qwen3-4B at 4x, raising performance on the discriminator dataset from 0.35 to 0.97, while also outperforming RULER-HARD (+0.77 pts). For context extension, GAL boosts Dual Chunk Attention from 0.20 to 0.90 on the discriminator dataset, while yielding gains on standard benchmarks(ScienceFiction (+6 pts) and PG19 32K (-0.33 PPL)). GAL thus provides a path toward autonomous goalpost setting and algorithmic improvement, where AI systems continually discover their own weaknesses and develop methods to overcome them.

papers.title_en: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
papers.authors: Hyunin Lee, Jinglue Xu, Jeffrey Seely, Donghyun Lee, Somayeh Sojoudi, Matei Zaharia, Yujin Tang
papers.evidence: 提出MASS，一种利用多智能体自我监督和自生成轨迹的递归自我改进方法。
papers.tldr: 在开放研究等不可验证任务上，模型输出已超出专家可评估范围，自我改进面临监督瓶颈，单一模型自评自改又难以突破同质循环。MASS 让同一基座模型反复提出、执行并自评多智能体工作流，在结构护栏约束下做进化搜索，并在自生成轨迹上做监督微调，两阶段交替进行。用 Qwen3.6-27B 跑两轮后，四个开放式公开基准上每输出 token 性能提升 1.2–1.6 倍。多智能体轨迹还更省训练量，表明联合学习编排与受限子智能体执行可为递归自我改进提供有效信号。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) of a model on non-verifiable tasks, such as open-ended research, faces a supervision bottleneck when its outputs exceed what even human experts can reliably assess, leaving the model itself (optimizee) as the best available optimizer and evaluator. However, a single model instance struggles to critique and improve its own complex reasoning under this homogeneous loop. To address this, we propose Multi-Agent Self-Supervision (MASS), an RSI method that alternates between evolutionary workflow optimization and supervised fine-tuning on self-generated trajectories. Guided by early findings that multi-agent topologies excel at complex reasoning, MASS prompts a single base model to iteratively propose, execute, and self-evaluate multi-agent workflows. Through an evolutionary search constrained by structural guardrails, the model optimizes these computational-graph-like orchestrations, discovering the most effective distinct roles and information routing for a given task. Over two MASS cycles with Qwen3.6-27B, the model achieves 1.2-1.6x higher performance per output tokens on four open-ended public benchmarks. Because the improved model subsequently acts as a better optimizer and evaluator, this alternating framework enables a continuous, recursive bootstrapping of the model's capabilities. Moreover, multi-agent traces are also more training-efficient: a student trained on them outperforms a single-agent student trained on 1.4x more training tokens. These findings suggest that jointly learning orchestration and bounded subagent execution from multi-agent trajectories can provide an effective signal for RSI.

papers.title_en: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
papers.authors: Ruiyao Xu, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Yifei Ming, Han Yu, Rujun Han, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister
papers.evidence: 自动演化智能体执行框架的递归自我改进框架
papers.tldr: LLM 智能体的能力不仅取决于模型，也取决于执行框架（harness），而递归自我改进可用于自动演化框架，但在开放世界任务中面临两个难题：测试时任务新颖且无真值验证器，且改进过程难以泛化。为此提出 Harness^2 双层递归框架：任务级用对比式 Propose-Probe-Compose 在无验证器下可靠引导编辑，框架级从编辑中提炼经验持续更新改进框架。在三个专业基准、四种模型-框架配置上，单步即稳定超越基线，最高提升 11.5、4.5 和 11.8 个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected levels of recursion. Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion. Harnessing-level recursion then extracts experience from these edits to update a continual improvement harness, enabling the agent to better adapt to future tasks. Across three professional benchmarks and four model-harness configurations, a single step consistently improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, yielding gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB, with further gains as the task-level recursion budget increases.

papers.title_en: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.authors: Leijun Zhou, Yanke Yu, Zhihao Liu, Qu Xiang, Tiancheng Hu, Yiru Dong, Yihan Wu, Yangxi Xiang, Xuejun Wu, Xi Chen, Buyue Qian, Yaowei Zheng, Junhao Hu
papers.evidence: 递归自我改进设计维度的统一分类体系
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进使语言智能体可保留对参数、记忆、技能和代码的修改，持续参与自身开发。论文从统一分类和传统深度学习机制两条视角梳理现有RSI方法：前者提出九维设计空间并讨论维度交互，后者连接优化、正则化、数据增强、持续学习、对抗学习与进化计算。文章还回顾在线、离线及离线到在线基准，旨在帮助研究者从既有设计与学习机制中提炼新的RSI研究思路。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a route to AI systems that participate in their own continued development. Recent methods allow language agents to retain changes to their parameters, memory, skills, and code for subsequent execution and improvement. We examine how these methods can inform new research ideas through two complementary perspectives. First, we introduce a unified taxonomy with nine design dimensions organized into four groups: update targets, update organization, update schedule and scope, feedback and selection. This taxonomy places existing methods in a shared design space, where examining individual dimensions and their interactions can inspire new research ideas. Second, we examine how existing RSI methods draw on traditional deep learning, for example through optimization, regularization, data augmentation, continual learning, and adversarial learning. We develop further ideas by examining more specific learning mechanisms and drawing on evolutionary computation. We also review how existing benchmarks assess self-improvement under online, offline, and offline-to-online settings. Together, these perspectives help researchers develop new RSI research ideas from existing designs and learning mechanisms. RSI papers and resources are available at https://prism-shadow.github.io/awesome-rsi/.

papers.title_en: Self-improving data synthesis enables scalable adaptation of embedding models
papers.authors: Zucan Lyu, Rui Tang, Jianlyu Chen, Peisheng Jin, Defu Lian
papers.evidence: 自改进智能体框架为嵌入模型自主合成训练数据
papers.tldr: 嵌入模型适配受限于人工训练数据设计，SYNTRA将少量检索示例转化为可复用合成指令。它基于无标注语料推断信息需求与相关性标准，并用试输出反馈迭代优化查询生成和相关性评估。在24个数据集15个领域上，同一流程能生成有效训练数据，六项任务自我改进均增强监督，四项优于人工校准。MS MARCO上合成数据量扩至32倍仍持续增益，展示低人工干预的可扩展适配路径。
papers.abstract_en: AI agents require specialised retrieval across domains and tasks, but adapting embedding models is constrained by costly manual training-data design. Here we introduce SYNTRA, a self-improving agentic framework that turns a few retrieval examples into reusable synthesis instructions. Given an unlabelled corpus and a few relevant query-document pairs, SYNTRA infers implicit information needs and relevance criteria, then uses feedback on trial outputs to refine instructions for query generation and relevance assessment. Experiments across 24 datasets spanning 15 domains demonstrate that the same synthesis workflow produces effective training data, benefiting even strong embedding models with and without existing labelled training sets. Self-improvement strengthens this supervision on all six evaluated tasks, yielding better retrieval than human calibration on four. The training value persists at larger scales: on MS MARCO, retrieval gains continue across a 32-fold range of synthetic training-data sizes. SYNTRA thus enables scalable embedding-model adaptation with minimal human intervention.

papers.title_en: Drafting Agents, Not Just Tokens: Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Systems
papers.authors: Xin Xu, Ke Cheng, Hao Wang, Yangru Huang, Yanghao Xiao, Zhichao Chen, Zhisheng Zhong, Xun Liu, Yi Li, Qian Li, Haibin Lv, Jun Zhang, Jie Jiang, Zhouchen Lin
papers.evidence: 推测式递归自我改进在预算约束下草拟并验证改进后的后继智能体
papers.tldr: 智能体逐版改进需在有限预算下兼顾探索与验证，窄搜索易漏编辑序列，逐版全评又会耗尽预算。SpecRSI先草拟可执行后继智能体、待完整验证后再采纳，并用VATS分配编辑与校验预算、GVO学习改进器。科学任务终端增益较Janus高33.3%–40.0%，在50个骨干—任务对全胜，编码验证成功率达69.4%。该框架将推测式递归自改进与验证感知搜索结合，为智能体自我进化提供更省预算的可靠路径。
papers.abstract_en: Improving an agent through successive revisions requires balancing exploration and evaluation under a limited budget. A narrow search can miss useful sequences of edits, while fully evaluating every intermediate version can exhaust the budget before those sequences yield a verified improvement. We introduce Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement (SpecRSI), which drafts executable successor agents before their predecessors are fully evaluated, while requiring complete verification before adoption. Verification-Aware Tree Search (VATS) allocates the budget between further edits and outstanding checks using the predicted verified return of a continuation. Group Verification Optimization (GVO) learns the improver from completed searches while keeping the real evaluator fixed. In the main scientific comparison, terminal gains exceed Janus by 33.3%--40.0%. Additional evaluations show that SpecRSI outperforms Janus in all 50 scientific backbone--task pairs and exceeds MetaRSI-v1 by 1.85%--2.38% in macro-average system score across twenty backbones. Coding-validation success reaches 69.4% versus HGM's 64.3% at a 20.8% lower target-cost index.

papers.title_en: AReaL-RSI: Adaptive Scaling and Coordination of Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.authors: Wenhao Zhou, Jiajun Song, Haitao Wang, Zipeng Qiu, Yingqi Peng, Ruida Xu, Jiale Li, Wenshuang Li, Shusheng Xu, Wei Dong, Hao Dai, Tongkai Yang, Yi Gao, Binhang Yuan
papers.evidence: 组织持久研究团队智能体并以结果与资源开销刻画扩展
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进规模化需持续算力，但多智能体并行易致早期评分失真、共享发现丢失适用条件、经验难复用。AReaL-RSI 不更新主干LLM权重，由领导者选择方向并指导探索，条件记忆共享区分未解问题与已验证发现，轮后基于证据复盘调整方向、知识与技能。实验对比Codex-Goal，两个主干均提升Terminal Bench 2.2个百分点，KernelBench平均加速提升32.2%至36.8%，经验共享加专用角色较独立探索降1.9%至27.5%内核延迟，为持久多智能体递归自我改进提供组织方案。
papers.abstract_en: Scaling recursive self-improvement requires additional computation to produce useful research progress in reaching persistent objectives. Intuitively, more researcher agents can explore more hypotheses, but early evaluation scores might misrepresent their promise, shared findings could lose their applicability conditions, and useful procedures could remain confined to completed investigations. In this paper, we present AReaL-RSI, a framework for organizing a persistent research team of agents without updating backbone LLM weights. We formulate the scaling problem in terms of evaluated outcomes and whole-system resource expenditure. Concretely, a leader agent selects task-appropriate research orientations and guides ongoing investigations; conditional memory sharing distinguishes unresolved problems from supported findings and enables recipient adaptation. During recursive evolution, after each campaign, evidence-based review revises researcher orientation, knowledge, and skills for later campaigns. Experiments compare AReaL-RSI with Codex-Goal on downstream harness optimization, GPU kernel optimization, and AI research tasks using two backbones. Under the reported resource allocations, AReaL-RSI improves Terminal Bench performance by 2.2 percentage points for each backbone and increases mean KernelBench speedup by 32.2-36.8%; further scalability comparisons favor the design of AReaL-RSI over native scaling: combining experience sharing with specialized researcher roles yields 1.9-27.5% lower kernel latency than independent exploration and 1.3-33.9% lower latency than sharing alone across all seven comparable task-backbone pairs.

papers.title_en: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.authors: Hai Zhou, Fan Yang, Zeyi Chen, Lejun Zhang, Chenyang Fu, Jianping Li, Jiayi Zhu, Xianyang Liu, Yingxuan Yang, Lili Meng, Lu Wang, Xinyang Han, Jiankai Sun, Weirui Ye, Guanchu Wang, Wanhua Li, Ming Zhou, Boyi Li, Ming Jin, Kun Shao, Muhao Chen, Guang Chen, Lei Ma, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Costas Spanos, Xia Hu, Mac Schwager, Weinan Zhang, Qian Feng, Shangding Gu
papers.evidence: 研究机器人同时更新能力与改进程序的物理递归自我改进
papers.tldr: 机器人任务执行日益自主，但其改进仍主要依赖人类，物理递归自我改进（Physical RSI）旨在让物理经验驱动能力与改进流程的持久更新。作者提出L0-L5框架，区分能力级与元级更新、任务内与跨任务收益，并梳理harness适配、模型训练及安全控制方法。分析发现现有文献尚未证明符合该定义的Physical RSI。论文据此指出可靠反馈、因果归因、安全保持与基准测试等优先方向，并给出开源仓库。
papers.abstract_en: Robots are increasingly autonomous in task execution, yet their improvement remains largely human-driven. This study investigates Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), in which physical experience guides lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its improvement procedure, making subsequent improvement more effective across tasks. Physical RSI faces challenges from noisy observations, continuous dynamics, costly trials, and irreversible consequences. We present an L0-L5 framework that differentiates capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, reserving L5 for independently verified recursive gain. We study existing methods around harness adaptation and model training, alongside safety and control mechanisms that govern execution and successive updates. Our analysis reveals that, despite substantial progress in self-improvement, the surveyed literature does not yet demonstrate Physical RSI as defined by our framework. We identify research priorities in reliable feedback, causal attribution, safety preservation, and benchmarking, outlining a path toward robots that autonomously improve how they learn while ensuring safety. The GitHub repository for Physical RSI is available at https://github.com/SAIL-Research-Lab/Physical-RSI.

papers.title_en: MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA
papers.authors: Junyi Zou, Avrova Donz
papers.evidence: 提出通过自我改进的适应方法更新策略与记忆的递归自我改进方案
papers.tldr: MMLA-RSI 面向未解决问题中的智能体递归自我改进，提出 RTT 改策略状态 Φ、RTMA 改权威记忆 M 两条路径，并让当前更新器或记忆管理器选择其继任者。方法给出有界规则语言、共享任务/提案接口和统一算法，由固定解释器、可信提交器与独立评估器约束变更。四候选程序选择中，保留 LARC 反馈使两种初始化期望误差分别降低 24.65 和 36.65 个百分点；连续集成回放显示反馈绑定为正但保留会增加损失。贡献是形式化两条递归路线及组合，有益递归链与发现效率仍待评估。
papers.abstract_en: An agent can improve its behavior within an unresolved problem by changing how it acts and which experience it retains. We propose MMLA-RSI, a recursive self-improvement scheme with two implementations in Memory-Mediated Learning Architecture: Reasoning-Time Training (RTT) changes the policy state $Φ$, while Reasoning-Time Memory Adaptation (RTMA) changes authoritative memory $M$. Each route also makes its adaptation method an object of improvement. A current numerical updater trains the policy proposing its successor; a current memory manager chooses the records available to the process proposing its successor. An independently admitted successor takes over the same role in the next generation. We give bounded executable rule languages, shared task/proposal interfaces, and one algorithm for either route or their composition. The RTT instance changes scalar schedules in a clipped-momentum update. The RTMA instance chooses NULL or a complete-row write with possible eviction. A fixed interpreter, trusted committer, and independent evaluator bound what can change. State versions, read closures, and conditional properties describe causal execution, accepted transitions, and finite work. Existing numerical-component studies motivate the construction. In four-candidate program selection, retaining LARC feedback updates reduces expected error by 24.65 and 36.65 percentage points for two trained initializations. In chronological continuous-integration replay, feedback binding is positive while retention increases loss. Completed SQL studies improve substantially over an unadapted substrate but do not establish the required additional online benefit. These results characterize their declared components. The two recursive routes and their joint realization are specified here; their beneficial recursive chains and discovery efficiency remain to be evaluated.

papers.title_en: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
papers.authors: Qianru Meng, Xi Zhang, Konstantinos Papakostas, Congfeng Cao, Wenxiang Hu, Tianyi Lu, Xiao Zhang, Lun Zhou, Zaiqiao Meng, Zhaochun Ren, Xiaohui Yan, Yougang Lyu
papers.evidence: 通过演化科学智能体群体实现递归自我改进
papers.tldr: 科学智能体群可通过实验经验递归自我改进，但实验结果不佳时难以判断该改假设还是实现，整体分数也会掩盖可复用组件。SwarmRSI 用反馈引导的群变异精炼假设与实现，并以互补群重组跨智能体复用保留假设和程序组件，再整合为递归群进化闭环。在 OpenProblems、NatureBench 和 MLE-Bench Lite 上取得 SOTA，且积累经验能提升留出任务表现，生物学家也复现其程序用于后续分析。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in scientific research aims to improve agents' research capabilities through their own experimental experience. Scientific agent swarms can combine evidence and implementations from different research directions to guide their agents' subsequent experiments. However, poor experimental results can leave unclear whether to revise a hypothesis or its implementation, while overall program scores can hide components useful to other agents. To address these challenges, we introduce SwarmRSI, a framework that evolves scientific agent swarms for recursive self-improvement. We devise Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation to refine hypotheses and their implementations using experimental feedback from other agents. We also propose Complementary Swarm Recombination to reuse retained hypotheses and complementary program components across agents, allowing partial results to support new research. Recursive Swarm Evolution integrates both mechanisms into a feedback loop, using new experimental evidence to guide subsequent research. Experiments on OpenProblems, NatureBench and MLE-Bench Lite demonstrate SwarmRSI's state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance. Further evaluations show that accumulated research experience improves performance on held-out tasks. Biologists also reproduce its programs for follow-up biological analyses.

papers.title_en: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
papers.authors: Peidong Wang, Ying Chang, Zhiming Ma, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng, Daqi Liu, Yuzhe Yang, Xu Cao, Chuang Wang, Jian Su, Daling Wang
papers.evidence: 按需递归自我改进，决定何时更新执行器权重
papers.tldr: 预训练VLA在未见长程任务中常中途失败，现有具身递归自改进难以判断该改调用框架还是执行器权重。AdaRSI先让编码智能体改进技能与harness，再从保存状态重试失败子步骤以归因，仅对仍不可靠的子步骤自采集演示微调。在RoboCasa365全部50个目标任务上，以GR00T N1.5为执行器且无人类演示，未见复合任务成功率从4.6%升至13.8%。该按需RSI以更少算力和演示取得更高成功率，强调先归因再改权重。
papers.abstract_en: Pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs) often fail midway through unseen long-horizon tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a remedy, but embodied RSI methods either refine the harness around a frozen executor and so cannot add a missing motion, or train the executor on persistent failures without asking whether a failure lies in how the executor is called or in what it can do. We ask when a self-improving embodied system should change the weights of its executor, and propose AdaRSI, an on-demand RSI framework for embodied agents. A coding agent first improves its skills and harness, then attributes persistent failures by retrying failing sub-steps from saved states, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable, with demonstrations it collects itself and experience carried over from earlier tasks. On all 50 target tasks of RoboCasa365, with GR00T N1.5 as the executor and no human demonstrations, AdaRSI improves the VLA on all three suites and raises its success on unseen composite tasks from 4.6% to 13.8%. Compared with fine-tuning every sub-step, it reaches slightly higher success while using only 28% of the GPU time and 22% of the self-collected demonstrations, and fine-tuning without a harness trains more yet gains far less.

papers.title_en: Recursive Reward Improvement via Adversarial Meta-Prompt Evolution
papers.authors: Wei Dai, Qianchu Liu, Guanghui Qin, Xing Han, Tristan Naumann, Paul Pu Liang, Sheng Zhang
papers.evidence: 利用提议者-求解者递归自我改进生成训练任务与评分量表，改进开放式专家任务的奖励。
papers.tldr: 开放专家任务缺少可自动核验的标准答案，自改进需模型自写评分细则，但细则常被solver钻空子，只列主题而无实质内容。RRI引入奖励攻击对抗者：先写钻rubric空子的无用答案，再让同一模型盲写诚实答案，并用至多两步修复使诚实答案胜出。HealthBench Professional上，RRI较仅生成基线在9B/27B提升10.9/12.4分，无外部模型也提升10.3分。发现的漏洞还会反馈到后续任务与细则生成，进而为开放式自博弈提供可监督的奖励改进路径。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) has gained wide attention for its ability to work with limited data. In a proposer-solver loop, a proposer model writes training tasks and a solver model learns to solve them through reinforcement learning. Such loops have succeeded in mathematics and coding, where every answer can be checked automatically. Open-ended expert tasks, like clinical report generations, have no answer key, which makes simple question-answer generation not viable. Here the proposer must also write a rubric that lists the content an answer should include and the errors it should avoid. However, the unique challenge behind model-written rubric is the comprehensiveness of it. For naively generated rubric, solvers tend to exploit it, naming the expected topics without the substance behind them, which corrupts the learning process. To solve this problem, we introduce RRI, Recursive Reward Improvement, which uses a reward hacking adversary to supervise the reward. Before the solver trains on a generated task, an adversary writes an answer that games its rubric while being as useless as possible, the same model writes an honest answer without seeing the rubric, and up to two repair steps revise the rubric to make the honest answer win. The exploits found also rewrite how future tasks and rubrics are generated. On HealthBench Professional, RRI improves the adjusted score over the Generation Only self-improvement baseline by 10.9 points at 9B and 12.4 at 27B, and by 10.3 points without any external model. In particular, the gains are largest on difficult and writing tasks. We show that the 27B model trained on the HealthBench Professional description improves by 6.6 points on PRBench Hard and 8.0 on ProfBench without seeing a task from either. We further analyze the exploitable points of model-generated question-rubric pairs to facilitate future research on open-ended self-play.

papers.title_en: Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research
papers.authors: Yufa Zhou, Yichen Wang, Jiakun Fan, Ziqi Shu, Zhichao Liu, Anru R. Zhang, Neiwen Ling, Zijun Wei
papers.evidence: 构建在真实GPU上进行自主后训练研究的智能体原生系统
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进难以直接测量，作者转而考察前沿智能体能否自主后训练小型基座模型。他们构建Athanor系统，提供沙箱、冻结评测、去污染数据与留出测试集，让四个智能体自主造数据、改算法、调参。104小时内Qwen3-4B-Base在开发集从15.9升至67.3，留出集从9.2升至48.2，追平官方Instruct。这首次证明智能体团队可自主完成跨域通用化后训练。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems build stronger AI systems, is one promising route to superintelligence. We study a weaker form that can be measured today: frontier agents post-training a small raw base model with public data, as a test of their research potential. We build Athanor, an open agent-native system for autonomous post-training research (AutoPostTrain) on real GPUs. We give the agents full research autonomy, low-friction engineering tools, and efficient starter code. The agents carry out the research themselves: they read datasets and evaluation results, build their training data, write and modify training algorithms, tune hyperparameters, and analyze the results to decide what to try next. They work in a sandbox and cannot use external teacher models. Athanor's services supply frozen evaluation, managed jobs, decontaminated data, a persistent research record, and a held-out suite the agents are unaware of. In a 104-hour campaign, a team of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents, each on an eight-GPU node and given no research advice, improves Qwen3-4B-Base from 15.9 to 67.3 on a six-task development suite and from 9.2 to 48.2 on a held-out suite, against 66.5 and 47.9 for the official Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a team of frontier agents can autonomously post-train a raw base model into a cross-domain generalist model that matches or surpasses the official instruct version on average. The campaign's full record shows that the agents reach this level by recombining known methods and each other's models: SFT on public reasoning data, RL with a rollout change one agent introduced, weight merges across agents, and rounds of self-distillation. With execution handled, today's agents already have the engineering and research ability to conquer this task. We hope Athanor provides a foundation for scaling autonomous AI research.

papers.title_en: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
papers.authors: Shangheng Du, Jinxin Shi, Shuaiyu Zhang, Yiming Wu, Junpeng Zhao, Shiyang Feng, Xin Li, Liang He, Xiangchao Yan, Bo Zhang
papers.evidence: 训练面向自主机器学习工程的通用智能体模型以推进AI4AI与递归自我改进
papers.tldr: 针对长周期机器学习工程中反馈稀疏、实验昂贵的问题，作者提出自主MLE后训练方法并训练35B MoE智能体MLExpert。其方法包括Kaggle-MLE Factory、分层智能体SFT，以及将相邻实验结果间的多轮决策作为执行窗口并共享结果奖励的WIRL。在MLE-Bench Lite上平均奖牌率从37.9%升至72.7%，接近更大前沿模型。该能力还可泛化到其他优化任务，为AI4AI提供实践路径。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

papers.title_en: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
papers.authors: Minhua Lin, Zijun Wang, Zewen Liu, Zhaotian Weng, Bing He, Zhan Shi, Benoit Dumoulin, Xiang Zhang, Suhang Wang, Hanqing Lu
papers.evidence: 语言模型学习自动化语言模型研发改进
papers.tldr: 大模型正被用于自动化语言模型研发，但用真实实验反馈训练“提出改进方案”的能力成本极高，且代理奖励易被策略利用而失真。LM2LM用强化学习训练模型生成改进提案，并以冻结LLM构成的RWM根据上下文实验记录预测增益作为奖励，定期真实执行高排名提案并回填结果以校准反馈。在八类自回归与扩散LM开发环境中，Qwen3.8-27B的真实执行表现超过可参考300条实验记录的GPT-6-sol，数据生成成本还低33%，并能泛化到训练未见模型族。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts. To address these challenges, we propose LM2LM, which trains LLMs with RL to generate effective LM improvement proposals. To provide scalable feedback, we use a research world model (RWM), a frozen LLM that predicts proposal gains from real experimental records provided in context, as the reward model for RL. To maintain feedback reliability, we periodically execute current-policy proposals ranked highly by the RWM and add their measured outcomes to its context. Across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments, real-execution evaluations on held-out tasks show that LM2LM enables Qwen3.8-27B to outperform GPT-6-sol, even when GPT-6-sol is given 300 real experimental records in context, while requiring 33% lower data-generation cost. LM2LM also generalizes to a model family unseen during training.

papers.title_en: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
papers.authors: Ruotian Peng, Yuanyi Ren, Shuaiqi Liu, Xin Guo, Fang Zhu, Yangyi Huang, Yue Wu, Zheng Wang, Yandong Wen, Zhihang Fu
papers.evidence: 面向RSI中数据训练器与推理框架协同设计的基准
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进要求智能体诊断系统瓶颈，并协同优化训练与推理。为此提出 VibeTraining-Bench，覆盖终端操作、软件工程、多轮工具使用与数学推理，让研究智能体在固定预算下迭代改进数据、训练器与推理框架并提交最终系统。结果显示前沿研究智能体可显著提升目标系统，如 SWE-bench Verified 上从 32.9% 升至 53.7%。该基准为推进 RSI 与跨组件协同优化提供统一平台。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires agents to diagnose system bottlenecks and coordinate improvements across training and inference. We refer to the agents' capability to jointly optimize training data, the trainer, and the inference harness as cross-component co-design. We introduce VibeTraining-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating this capability across tasks spanning terminal operation, software engineering, multi-turn tool use, and mathematical reasoning. Within each task, research agents start from an identical initial agent system under a fixed resource budget. Guided by validation feedback, they iteratively refine data, trainers, and inference harnesses, then select and submit a final agent system for evaluation on the test set. To prevent reward hacking, we enforce three safeguards: test data isolation, separate research and grading containers, and network restrictions for research agents. Our evaluation results show that frontier research agents substantially improve target agent systems. For example, on SWE-bench Verified, GPT-6-Astra raises the target agent system's performance from 32.9% to 53.7%, comparable to the human-developed instruct model's 55.4%. However, there is still room to improve their ability to co-design and iteratively refine data, trainer, and harness to achieve cumulative performance gains. We hope that VibeTraining-Bench will serve as a unified platform for advancing RSI, deepening our understanding of cross-component optimization for agent systems. Code and data are available at https://github.com/D2I-ai/VibeTraining-Bench.

papers.title_en: MaD-RSI: Model-as-Data for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
papers.authors: Yu Cui, Hong He, Ruiqing Yue, Sicheng Pan, Zhuoyu Sun, Yifei Liu, Ting Li, Wenzhuo Zhu, Baohan Huang, Haibin Zhang, Cong Zuo
papers.evidence: 通过递归自我改进优化智能体框架，并关注适配新LLM的耦合问题与计算成本。
papers.tldr: 现有面向智能体框架的递归自我改进方法通常针对单一LLM搜索harness，易与目标模型强耦合，跨模型泛化差且适配新模型成本高。本文提出“模型即数据”视角与MaD-RSI框架，将多个异构LLM的多样化失败轨迹作为训练证据，联合优化共享harness。作者还设计了含两项互补指标的新评估框架，并在多数据集和多LLM上验证。结果显示，该方法在提升跨模型泛化能力的同时降低了训练成本。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) of agent harnesses has emerged as an effective approach to enhancing the capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents. By searching the harness space for a specific LLM on a given dataset, RSI can discover a harness tailored to the capabilities and behavioral characteristics of that model. However, such optimization often creates a strong coupling between the learned harness and its target LLM, limiting generalization across models and requiring substantial computational resources to adapt to new LLMs. Moreover, existing RSI methods typically optimize a harness using feedback from a single model and evaluate its generalization to other models only after training. This paradigm treats model differences primarily as a criterion for evaluating generalization rather than as valuable evidence for optimization. In this paper, we introduce a new perspective that treats models as data and places the harness at the center of optimization. Building on this perspective, we propose \textsc{MaD-RSI}, a framework that directly optimizes a shared harness across multiple heterogeneous LLMs by incorporating their diverse failure trajectories into the training process. Rather than assessing model differences only after optimization, \textsc{MaD-RSI} leverages these differences as training evidence to guide the self-improvement of a shared harness. Furthermore, we introduce a new evaluation framework with two complementary metrics designed to assess the effectiveness of harness optimization across models. Experiments across multiple datasets and LLMs demonstrate that \textsc{MaD-RSI} improves generalization over existing approaches while reducing training costs.

papers.title_en: RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training
papers.authors: Binghang Lu, Yige Sun, Guang Lin
papers.evidence: 元智能体在递归自我改进循环中跨轮重写优化器策略
papers.tldr: 传统神经网络训练依赖预设优化配方，固定LLM代理难跨运行积累经验。RSI-Opt让元代理依据历史证据改写提示、流程手册、优化器代码库与决策节奏，并用存档保留已评估策略。五代演化在三项任务上提升代理性能，Opus 5.5演化套件z分数由+10.48升至+14.33，GPT-5.5跨模型迁移在留出任务由-0.36升至+3.11。Burgers PDE上相对L2误差较固定提示基线降低约2.7倍与8.8倍，显示可复用程序与工具能支持科学机器学习迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Conventional neural-network training typically follows a predefined optimization recipe, motivating a LLM agent that monitors training dynamics and adjusts optimizer settings as training progresses, but a fixed agent policy does not accumulate experience across runs. We introduce RSI-Opt, a plug-and-play Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents which evolves the knowledge that guides this process: a prompt, a playbook of procedures, a library of tested optimizer code, and a decision cadence. A meta-agent rewrites this policy using evidence from earlier runs, and an archive retains evaluated policies for further evolution. Across 5 generations on three training tasks, the meta-agents develop reusable procedures and code and conduct their own CPU proxy experiments. RSI-Opt substantially improves optimizer-agent performance, with representative raw-space summary $z$-scores increasing from $+10.48$ to $+14.33$ on the evolution suite with Opus 5.5 and from $-0.36$ to $+3.11$ on held-out tasks with GPT-5.5 through cross-model policy transfer. On the Burgers PDE, it reduces mean relative $L_2$ error by approximately 2.7-fold with Opus 5.5 and 8.8-fold with GPT-6.1 over the fixed-prompt agent baseline, although PDE transfer varies across LLMs and tasks. Controlled comparisons show that the evolved policy combines reusable optimization knowledge with adaptation to each task: initial decisions capture most observed gains on seen tasks, while continued adaptation improves outcomes on unseen tasks. These findings demonstrate how procedures and executable tools accumulated across training runs can improve optimizer-agent performance and support transfer to scientific machine learning.

papers.title_en: ParetoRSI-Gym: Can AI Agents Improve Language Models Across Multiple Domains?
papers.authors: Haojin Wang, Yangzhen Wu, Zeyi Chen, Jian Xie, Jiaying Ye, Lili Meng, Shuyun Tang, Shangding Gu, Dawn Song
papers.evidence: 多领域评测智能体驱动的RSI后训练
papers.tldr: 现有递归自我改进评测多在单一基准上进行，难以衡量跨领域取舍。ParetoRSI-Gym让智能体在固定初始模型、五领域、工具集与SFT流程下，反复搜数据、筛选、训练并读取分领域结果，同时用泛化基准区分能力提升与过拟合。最强系统Claude Code搭配Opus-5使其代理最优检查点泛化分相对起点提升9.2%，单领域最高提升63%。该工作将RSI评测推进到多领域真实机器学习工程。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agentic system to design, train, and evaluate its own successor. Data-driven post-training is a central part of that loop, yet existing evaluations measure it on a single benchmark, where an agent selects from a static pool or distills a stronger model to push one score up in one run. Real post-training is multi-domain, and a gain in one domain has to be weighed against a regression in another. We propose ParetoRSI-Gym, in which an agent searches for data, curates it, trains, reads back per-domain results, and repeats, with everything but the data held fixed: the initial LLM, the five domains (math, code, finance, medicine, science), the toolset, and the SFT pipeline. Generalization benchmarks in each domain separate capability gains from overfitting to the scores the agent optimizes against. Across three agent systems, three base models, five rounds and multiple seeds, the strongest system, Claude Code with Opus-5, raises the generalization scores of its proxy-best checkpoint by 9.2% relative to the starting model (+2.3 absolute points), averaged with equal weight over three base models and five domains, with a single-domain relative gain of up to 63% (medicine on Ministral-3-3B). Further analysis shows that the harness matters as much as the model it drives, and that each agent keeps a unique data selection strategy. We see our work as a step towards evaluation of RSI systems in real-world machine learning engineering.

papers.title_en: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
papers.authors: Jiayue Pu, Ang Gao, Jinyi Bai, Qipeng Wang, Tongyu Wen, Jiahao Zhao, Keyu Qu, Junhao Zhang, Chenglei Shen, Zhongxiang Sun, Jun Xu, Xiao Zhang
papers.evidence: 分析如何区分可信的自我修改增益与评测缺陷及继承能力
papers.tldr: 大模型系统借助反馈持续修改模型、提示、记忆与工具，但自我修改不等于可信改进。本文给出递归自我改进的操作定义与流程框架，从改进有效性、约束保持和有效监督三视角梳理四类可信要求。综述覆盖S1–S4及改进机制递归修订的风险、防护与评估证据，并区分直接发现与相关系统证据。最后提出独立、纵向评估需求与开放问题，为可信RSI研究与治理提供路线图。
papers.abstract_en: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or sensitive information may also persist in successor systems. Changes to improvement mechanisms may invalidate earlier verification results and make human oversight less effective. This survey presents an operational definition and process framework for RSI and organizes the requirements for trustworthy RSI into four interconnected themes: genuine and sustained improvement; behavioral constraints, alignment, and fairness; system security and privacy; and transparency and controllability. We examine these themes from three perspectives: Improvement Validity, Constraint Preservation, and Effective Oversight. This analysis covers improvement diagnosis, proposal generation, proposal evaluation, and update implementation (S1--S4), including the recursive application of these stages to improvement mechanisms (RI). We review risks, safeguards, and evaluation evidence for individual updates, effects inherited by successor systems, and revisions to improvement mechanisms, while distinguishing direct RSI findings from evidence in related systems. Finally, we examine evaluation settings, identify requirements for independent and longitudinal assessment, and discuss applications and open research problems.

papers.title_en: Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
papers.authors: Wangcheng Tao, Zhanglu Yan, Han Wu, Weng-Fai Wong
papers.evidence: 直接提出通过自我优化的元技能实现智能体技能的递归自我改进。
papers.tldr: 现有技能优化器多依赖手工设计流程，即便演化元技能也局限于固定管线并需逐任务重学。Skill∞ 让元智能体按元技能优化任务技能，并用同一过程递归优化元技能，诊断轨迹、提出候选、请求独立评审并分配搜索预算。元技能与任务技能解耦，可跨多个优化任务精炼后复用到不同领域。在83个SkillsBench任务上通过率达60.7%，高于人工技能56.4%与SkillEvolver 54.5%。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI), in which a system also improves the way it improves, is a long-standing aspiration on the path to AGI. Language agents increasingly store procedural knowledge in reusable skills. Optimizing skills offers a direct way to achieve RSI, because the optimization procedure itself can be encoded as a skill. Existing skill optimizers, however, follow a hand-designed procedure. Even methods that evolve a meta-skill confine it to a fixed pipeline and relearn it for each task. We present Skill$^{\infty}$, which makes skill optimization recursively self-improving: a meta agent follows a meta-skill to optimize task skills and optimizes the meta-skill itself using the same procedure. The optimization is agent-led. The meta agent diagnoses execution traces, proposes candidates, requests independent reviews, and allocates the search budget. The meta-skill defines these steps, allowing self-improvement to rewrite them. This meta-skill is also decoupled from task skills, refined on multiple skill optimization tasks and then reused to optimize task skills across diverse domains. As in deployment, skills at both levels are standard packages loaded through native skill discovery. On 83 SkillsBench tasks, Skill$^{\infty}$ reaches a pass rate of 60.7%, compared with 56.4% for human-curated skills and 54.5% for SkillEvolver.

papers.title_en: ReSAIL: Mitigating Collapse in Iterative Agent Self-Distillation
papers.authors: Shengjie Jin, Hengbo Xu, Zelong Sun, YuJie Guo, Zhiwu Lu
papers.evidence: 迭代智能体自蒸馏作为通往递归自我改进的路径
papers.tldr: 迭代式智能体自蒸馏有望推动递归自我改进，但现有方法在多轮部署中会出现性能坍塌，且依赖特权信息（PI）的任务表现同步下降。ReSAIL作为即插即用增强，优先选择PI最能改变教师预测的交互步，并平衡轨迹间的蒸馏损失，同时将学生的PI条件输出分布正则到冻结教师，以保留下一轮监督行为。在ALFWorld与TextCraft上，它跨模型规模、连续三轮维持显著增益，最终轮成功率平均绝对提升22.5%。该工作首次表明更稳健的学习机制可缓解迭代智能体自蒸馏的部署坍塌。
papers.abstract_en: Iterative self-distillation enables LLM agents to learn from successive deployments, offering a path toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet our experiments with existing methods reveal a collapse in deployment performance across cycles, while task performance with privileged information (PI) also declines. We address this collapse by prioritizing informative interaction steps for distillation and preserving PI-conditioned behavior as the student becomes the next teacher. We introduce Retentive and Selective Augmentation for Iterative Self-Distillation (ReSAIL), a plug-in augmentation for iterative PI-based self-distillation. ReSAIL selects interaction steps where PI most strongly changes the teacher's predictions and balances the resulting distillation losses across trajectories. It also regularizes the student's PI-conditioned output distributions toward those of the frozen teacher at selected and unselected steps to preserve PI-conditioned behavior for supervision in the next cycle. On ALFWorld and TextCraft, ReSAIL sustains substantial gains across model scales over three cycles, with an average absolute gain of 22.5% in final-cycle success rates when added to self-distillation baselines. Sensitivity-guided selection of offline data also improves action prediction accuracy for multimodal GUI agents on AITZ. These findings provide the first evidence that a more robust learning mechanism can effectively mitigate performance collapse in iterative agent self-distillation over deployment trajectories.

papers.title_en: Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover
papers.authors: Yunbei Zhang, Janet Wang, Saiyue Lyu, Yingqiang Ge, Kaiqu Liang, Zijian Jin, Chandan K Reddy, Jihun Hamm
papers.evidence: 研究不安全改动为何在递归自我改进代际间持续及智能体如何恢复
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进让智能体跨代继承修改，但安全失败可能随之固化。作者构建有状态授权任务测试台，用固定LLM编辑器修改可执行组件，并通过配对干预分离验证、运行与下一轮编辑对象。结果显示，依赖更新后历史分数在48条轨迹中有22条保留了不安全程序，刷新分数可恢复正确性但独立测试仍有残余失败；完整验证与经验证回滚可在核心实验中实现全正确并保留逾43%部署节省。安全需检查当前条件下实际运行的程序，并选择下一个要编辑的实现。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) allows agents to carry useful changes across generations. Maintaining safety across these generations involves both preventing unsafe behavior from persisting and enabling recovery when failures occur. We study these challenges through a controlled testbed of stateful authorization tasks, where fixed LLM editors optimize executable agent components and independent traces record their effects. Paired interventions separate which revisions pass validation, which program continues running, and which program the editor revises next. After a new authorization dependency invalidates previously tested optimizations, historical scores preserve the same unsafe programs in 22 of 48 framework histories despite a correct alternative in every affected archive. Refreshing scores restores correctness on the original suite, with residual failures on independently composed tests. Failures also persist under an unchanged contract when all proposals are rejected and the failed incumbent remains active. Starting from shared failures, editing the initial implementation instead of the failed one improves recovery, although the advantage varies across editors. Full validation and validated rollback end with fully correct programs in the core trajectory study while retaining over 43% deployment savings. Preserving agent safety requires checking what will run under current conditions and choosing which implementation to edit next.

papers.title_en: Assembling Insights for Agentic Machine Learning Engineering Systems
papers.authors: Bihui Jin, Yinxi Li, Kaiyuan Wang, Pengyu Nie
papers.evidence: 系统研究相关任务洞见如何提升智能体化机器学习工程，是通向递归自我改进的一步
papers.tldr: 针对智能体机器学习工程中相关任务洞见收集与注入方式零散、评估存在数据泄漏的问题，作者提出MLE-InsightBench基准与MLE-InsightForge洞见组装智能体。该基准覆盖12个领域160个Kaggle竞赛，每领域留出1个目标赛，仅用148个无泄漏来源赛。系统从人类方案与写作中构建领域、竞赛和改进三类洞见，并以技能或手册注入。实验显示洞见使归一化私有测试分数较无洞见基线提升123.9%，三类洞见互补，技能注入整体更具性价比且收益可跨后端大模型泛化。
papers.abstract_en: Agentic machine learning engineering (MLE) is an emerging AI4SE application for complex ML tasks and a step toward recursive self-improvement of AI systems. Recent agentic MLE systems show the value of leveraging insights from related MLE tasks: some systems condition code generation on expert domain knowledge, which is implicitly curated from peer MLE tasks; some systems have a loop of solving an MLE task, gathering memory to benefit future tasks. However, insight collection and injection remain ad hoc, and existing evaluations often do not control insight sources, making data leakage a threat to validity.   To close these gaps, we systematically study how insights from related MLE tasks affect agentic MLE systems, and how their impact depends on insight type and injection method. We introduce MLE-InsightBench, a benchmark of 160 Kaggle competitions across 12 domains. To prevent leakage, one competition per domain is held out as the target, while the remaining 148 serve as sources only when they cannot have been influenced by the target task, such as through later editions or reused solutions. We also develop MLE-InsightForge, an insight assembly agent that explores source competitions, top human solutions, and writeups to construct three insight types: 12 domain insights summarizing best practices, 148 competition insights describing winning solutions, and 16 improvement insights capturing generic debugging and optimization strategies. These insights are injected either as on-demand skills or as an upfront playbook. In our evaluation, the extracted insights improve the normalized private-test score by 123.9% over a no-insight baseline. Controlled experiments further show that the three insight types are complementary; the better injection mode (skill vs. playbook) varies by tasks, with skills more cost-effective overall; and the gains generalize across backend LLMs.

papers.title_en: Second-Order Problem Solving for Recursive Self-Improvement in Formal Verification
papers.authors: Yuxuan Jiang, Aditya Vempaty, Ashish Jagmohan
papers.evidence: 面向工作流优化的二阶诊断式RSI
papers.tldr: 标准递归自我改进常作为一阶优化器，只针对即时失败症状反复修补参数，易陷入试错震荡且难解决底层机制。SO-RSI将工作流优化提升为二阶诊断式探究，先通过执行轨迹监测复发、相反编辑和期望不匹配三类结构异常，再触发轻量诊断探针并维护持久询问记忆。在Lean 4证明生成和Verus可验证代码生成中，匹配24小时预算下，最终留出通过率较Naive RSI分别提升21.8和25.8个百分点。该工作表明先诊断机制再结构干预可抑制失败复发并消除零进展循环。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) enables agents to iteratively optimize their workflows via execution feedback. However, standard RSI typically operates as a first-order optimizer: it repeatedly patches surface-level parameters in response to immediate failure symptoms, often leading to trial-and-error thrashing without resolving underlying mechanisms. To address this limitation, we introduce SO-RSI, a framework that elevates workflow optimization to a second-order diagnostic inquiry, investigating why failures occur before committing to structural interventions. SO-RSI passively monitors execution traces for three structural anomalies (recurrence, opposing edits, and expectation mismatch) to trigger targeted mechanism investigations. By executing lightweight diagnostic probes and maintaining persistent inquiry memory across RSI rounds, SO-RSI accumulates causal evidence to guide systematic workflow edits rather than parameter patches. Across Lean 4 proof generation and Verus-based verifiable code generation, SO-RSI improves final held-out pass rates over Naive RSI by 21.8 and 25.8 percentage points under matched 24-hour search budgets. Behavioral analyses further confirm that SO-RSI substantially suppresses failure recurrence and eliminates unproductive zero-progress optimization loops.

papers.title_en: Agent Plasticity: Measuring Self-Improvement Through Experience
papers.authors: Harman Singh, Anton Bakhtin, Rulin Shao, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ilia Kulikov, Rob Fergus, Sanjeev Arora, Kurt Keutzer, Jason Weston, Anuj Mahajan, Anirudh Goyal
papers.evidence: 通过经验衡量自我改进并分析效率与失效点
papers.tldr: 现有评测多衡量智能体在某一时点的能力，而非其从经验中学习的效率。作者在受控环境中让智能体把过往经验固化为可复用工件并传给后续实例，在训练与留出交互上计入学习成本，提出“智能体可塑性”衡量经验转化为未来留出性能增益的效率。多环境结果显示，前沿模型改进轨迹差异显著，分布外迁移仅部分成功，最终能力最强与学习效率最高并不一致，且失败瓶颈可分为不复用工件与复用后仍失败两类。
papers.abstract_en: AI agents increasingly operate in environments where they can diagnose failures and improve through experience, yet existing evaluations largely measure what an agent can do at a fixed point in time rather than how effectively it learns. Evaluating self-improvement requires answering three questions: does future performance improve and generalize beyond the interactions that enabled learning; how efficiently are new capabilities acquired; and where does the self-improvement process break down? To answer these questions, we study self-improvement in a controlled setting where agents amortize past experience into reusable artifacts that are inherited by future instances. At each checkpoint, we measure performance on training and held-out environment interactions while accounting for learning cost. We introduce agent plasticity, the efficiency with which an agent converts experience into gains in future held-out performance. Across multiple environments, frontier models exhibit sharply different improvement trajectories despite comparable opportunities to learn. Some achieve substantial and persistent gains, while others remain near or below their initial performance, and gains within the training regime often transfer only partially to out-of-distribution conditions. Endpoint capability and acquisition efficiency also diverge: the agent that ultimately performs best need not be the one that improves most efficiently. Tracing failures through the improvement loop further reveals different candidate bottlenecks. Agents with low plasticity often fail to reuse relevant artifacts, whereas more plastic agents may still fail despite reusing relevant artifacts, pointing to limitations in artifact quality, generalization, or application. Evaluating self-improving agents requires measuring not only what they can do, but how effectively they become better through experience.

papers.title_en: Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents
papers.authors: TianYi Lyu, Xiaozhe Li, Yang Li, Yongkang Chen, Kefei Tian, Junbo Niu, Zican Hu, Hongbo Liu, Mingliang Xiong, Qingwen Liu
papers.evidence: 训练递归语言模型智能体联合学习任务分解、求解与自我评估，支持自主能力提升。
papers.tldr: 递归语言模型智能体通过分解任务并委托子智能体形成工作树，但中间子任务缺少真值，逐节点调用验证器成本高且难以评估分解质量。SERA 让同一策略同时学习分解、求解与评估：父节点在委托前为子任务生成加权评分标准，并用最终可验证结果训练该评分标准与真实成功对齐。实验显示，训练生成对齐评分标准是主要增益来源，在 TextCraft-Synth 和 TextWorld-Sync 上平均提升 5.38 与 13.14 分。学习到的评分标准还可用于推理时树搜索选择，进一步提升性能。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive language-model agents decompose tasks and delegate subtasks to child instances of the same policy, forming a tree of work. Training them, however, is hard: the final outcome is verifiable, but the self-invented intermediate subtasks are numerous and carry no ground truth. Existing methods score each node with a verifier or judge, which is costly at scale and blind to decomposition quality. We argue that a recursive agent must learn three coupled capabilities within one set of weights: decomposing problems into subtasks, solving them, and evaluating the outcomes, each requiring its own training signal. SERA (Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents) turns evaluation into a learned capability of the policy itself. Before delegating, the parent writes a rubric of weighted success criteria for each child subtask; a ranking objective against verified outcomes then trains rubric generation so that the criteria track genuine subtask success. In addition, a complementary leaf-coverage signal provides direct credit for task decomposition. Our central finding is that \emph{training} the policy to generate aligned rubrics is what drives the gains: because the same weights both evaluate and execute, learning to judge subtasks sharpens the agent's ability to solve them. Notably, external supervision is also reduced: the judge is consulted only to train the rubric generator, while solving is trained against the agent's own rubric scores, which outperform direct use of the judge. Beyond training, the learned rubric doubles as an inference-time selector for tree search. On TextCraft-Synth and TextWorld-Sync, SERA improves over strong recursive-agent baselines by 5.38 and 13.14 points on average, and rubric-guided tree search at inference adds a further 2.43 points on TextWorld-Sync.

papers.title_en: DataSense-Bench: The First Step Toward an AI Scientist
papers.authors: Yudi Zhang, Mingyu Cao, Lu Yin, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Shiwei Liu
papers.evidence: 评测AI智能体自主选择训练数据以支撑机器学习研究
papers.tldr: 针对前沿AI是否具备“数据感”及能否可靠选择训练数据的问题，作者提出DataSense-Bench，让智能体检查数据、编写分析代码并做前向推理，对候选训练子集进行选择与排序，再以标准化微调评估其实际价值。实验覆盖终端问题求解与工具使用任务，发现相对随机选择的数据增益有限，智能体排序能力不稳定，Astra在三次工具使用中均选出最佳组，但终端任务三次仅一次成功。该基准将数据选择与性能预测纳入可复现评测，为AI科学家能力研究提供第一步。
papers.abstract_en: As claims about recursive self-improvement (RSI) and artificial general intelligence (AGI) proliferate, we ask a simple question: do frontier AI models have a sense of data, i.e., can they reliably select the right data for training? We introduce DataSense-Bench to study this capability through the fundamental problem of data selection and performance forecasting in machine learning. We ask AI agents to select and rank candidate training subsets that can be used to fine-tune a small LLM model. Agents are allowed to inspect the data, write and execute analysis code, and run model forward passes, but can not train the model or access the actual evaluation tasks. We then fine-tune the base model on each selected subset and evaluate its post-training performance under a standardized protocol. We instantiate the benchmark in terminal problem solving and tool use, selecting trajectories from OpenThoughts-Agent and EnvScaler and evaluating on TBLite and BFCL, respectively. We then evaluate the agents along two complementary dimensions: the post-training performance of the top-ranked subset, reflecting the ability to identify high-value training data, and ranking accuracy, reflecting the ability to predict the relative performance of the selected subsets. In our experiments, selection gains over random selection are limited; agents do not reliably rank their selected groups, and ranking ability does not hold consistently across tasks: Astra identifies the best group in all three tool-use runs but in only one of three terminal runs. Analysis of execution traces on both tasks shows that agents often use similar data signals while interpreting their training value differently.

papers.title_en: APT: Feedback-Driven Agentic Post-Training for Text-to-Image Generation
papers.authors: Sirui Zhang, Fangyun Wei, Dong Chen, Jinjing Zhao, Yitong Wang, Yunuo Chen, Baining Guo, Zheng-Jun Zha
papers.evidence: 自动生成评估与强化学习数据的智能体式后训练
papers.tldr: 现有文生图后训练多依赖人工整理数据和固定训练分布，难以随模型能力演化自适应调整。APT 用三个智能体自动构建评测集、诊断模型强弱与失败模式，并生成强调薄弱能力的强化学习数据。通过反复评测、诊断和更新生成器，当前模型行为会塑造下一轮训练任务，形成递归自我改进闭环。实验表明该方法跨模型、基准和生成架构均有效且全自动。
papers.abstract_en: Post-training is crucial for improving text-to-image models, yet existing pipelines typically rely on manually curated training data and fixed training distributions. We introduce APT (Agentic Post-Training), a fully automated framework that adaptively post-trains a base model according to its evolving capability profile.
